chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdul Kareem from Al-Halby who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I lease the land for a third or a quarter, so I sub-lease it for half.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it.' I said, 'Suppose I lease it for a thousand dirhams and sub-lease it for two thousand?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'It is not allowed.' I said, 'How did the first become allowed and the second not allowed?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Because this is guaranteed, and that is not guaranteed.'

key_terms.تَقَبُّل: To lease or take on lease

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between leasing for produce and leasing for money in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) in Islamic leasing contracts by distinguishing between share-based leases (*muzara'ah*), where the output is naturally uncertain, and fixed-rent leases, where the obligation is guaranteed. Scholars highlight that sub-leasing a share-based lease for a larger share is permissible because the lessee does not guarantee a specific yield, whereas sub-leasing a fixed-rent lease for double the amount is impermissible due to the mismatch in risk and guarantee (*daman*). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on aligning risk with reward to ensure contractual fairness.

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad from Abdul Kareem, from Al Halby who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The land is leased for a third (of the produce), or the quarter, so it is sub-leased for the half’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’. I said, ‘Supposing it is leased for a thousand Dirhams and sub-leased it for two thousand?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Not allowed’. I said, ‘How come the first is allowed and the second is not allowed?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because this is guaranteed, and that is without a guarantee’.
en.sarwar: 6. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd al-Karim from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about leasing saying, ‘Ther

e is a piece of land and it leased for one-third or one-fourth, then to someone else for one-half.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if I lease for one thousand dirhams and then lease it to someone else for two thousand dirhams?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not lawful.’ I then asked, ‘How is it that it is lawful in the first case and unlawful in the second case?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because in this case it is guaranteed and in that case it is not guaranteed.’”
